Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: BrightPath - integrated hosting: implementation questions & exception worksheet

Team —

Attaching the filled exception worksheet BrightPath sent through. They'd like a VPC + partial on-prem hosting model for sensitive PHI workloads and have asked us to confirm if we can meet the following by pilot kickoff (target: Feb 15):

- runtime isolation within customer VPC (control-plane vs data-plane split)
- support for local HSM/KMS chaining for key material
- ability to run inference on-prem for a small GPU fleet with our runtime image
- audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM (TLS/Mutual TLS)

Please review the worksheet and call out any absolute blockers, plus the minimal cross-functional work required to complete a pilot. Specifically I need technical constraints from infra/arch and an ops-oncall + support model estimate.

Actions requested by EOD Thursday:
- Karthik: complete architecture feasibility rows (networking, routing, failover)
- Soojin: list runbook / oncall gaps and staffing estimate
- Grace: procurement/AM ask — what contractual exceptions do we need and who signs off?

Attachment: brightpath_exception_worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-30T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightPath - integrated hosting: implementation questions & exception worksheet

Thanks Dylan — quick read-through and a few questions / notes inline below. I'll update the architecture sheet once we align on these.

1) VPC/data-plane split: feasible but requires a lightweight customer side network agent and a NAT/proxy pair in their VPC for routing encrypted RPC. Are we OK with maintaining a small customer-managed agent (Linux container) in the pilot? If not, we'll need to scope a managed gateway.

2) KV cache/weights: on-prem inference requires us to ship model artifacts into customer infra. We need a signed manifest + attestation flow. Does BrightPath have an internal registry or would they want us to host an air-gapped transfer package?

3) HSM/KMS chaining: we can support envelope encryption where customer KMS wraps our keys; full HSM integration (PKCS#11) will add ~3-4 sprints of engineering and requires security review. For pilot, recommend KMS chaining rather than direct HSM pulls.

4) Audit logs: we can stream structured logs to an endpoint; mutual TLS + client certs will be required. Ops: is there capacity to manage cert rotation for pilot customers?

5) Failure modes: if on-prem nodes are overloaded we can failover to hosted instances but that changes data residency guarantees. We should capture a fallback policy in the worksheet.

I'll add explicit diagrams to the sheet. Need answers to (2) and (4) to finalize the architecture rows.

-Karthik
Principal Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BrightPath - integrated hosting: implementation questions & exception worksheet

Fwding initial ops notes and a draft runbook I started for the pilot. High level:

- Oncall/Support: Pilot will need 2x oncall rotations (primary + backup) with SLOs defined per region. We don't have dedicated private-deploy oncall staff in us-west; current plan uses cross-trained infra oncall which will add ~0.4 FTE during pilot.

- Runbook gaps: orchestration for model artifact refresh, local cache warming, and emergency key-rotation steps are missing. I attached the draft runbook.

- Certs: we can automate cert issuance via our CA, but for customer-managed endpoints we need manual CSR approval per pilot customer (~1 day admin work).

- Attachments and references: ops_runbook_draft.md (attached). Also adding a link to a short checklist in Drive.

Open questions for architecture: do we want failover to hosted for JOINT workloads, or make it manual cutover? Automatic failover simplifies UX but conflicts with some residency constraints BrightPath listed.

I'll update the staffing table in the worksheet after Karthik answers the artifact delivery question.

—SoJin
Head of Platform Ops | Redwood Inference

Good thread — short summary and next steps from procurement/AM side: 

1) Contract exceptions: BrightPath is asking for an amendment to our data residency clause and a narrower indemnity for on-prem operations. Legal has flagged the indemnity as high risk; procurement recommends we offer a scoped addendum limited to the pilot (30 days after pilot ends) with a maximum liability cap. I'll engage Legal for a fast review — target response by Dec 9.

2) Approvals: Head of Sales must approve pilot credit + commercial concessions; Finance must sign off on liability cap. I will coordinate a short decision call next week with Sales/Finance/Legal.

3) Decision matrix items for the call: (a) Karthik to confirm artifact transport strategy, (b) Soojin to confirm FTE and runbook readiness, (c) Dylan to produce an engineer-facing one-page describing the rollback/failover policy for customer approval.

I will pull together the short decision packet and invite stakeholders. If we can align on the three matrix items we should be able to sign a pilot addendum quickly.

-Grace
Director, Technical Account Management | Redwood Inference
